morphology_keys.leaf_arrangement: Irregularly arranged, alternate to subopposite (occasionally opposite); do not treat apparently opposite leaves as a definitive identification character.
morphology_keys.leaf_morphology: Usually broad oblong to ovate (sometimes lanceolate), approximately 1–6 cm wide; tip obtuse/rounded to shortly acute, entire margins sometimes gently wavy.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Crowded terminal umbel-like clusters; additional lateral umbels may occur at a few upper nodes. Both this species and A. asperula can make dense clusters, so cluster looseness alone is unreliable.
morphology_keys.flower_color: Pale-green corolla lobes surrounding a corona with frequently rose to purplish-red hoods; colors vary.
morphology_keys.gynostegium_detail: Five pouch-like corona hoods are present. They lack a clearly projecting horn; an incipient horn/rudiment may be visible within a hood pocket (UT Williamson County description). Corona segments are generally less than half the length of the pale-green corolla lobes (Flora of North America comparison).
morphology_keys.growth_habit: Perennial with stems spreading or decumbent to ascending, sometimes upright, often to roughly 50–60 cm; habit alone overlaps with A. asperula.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Look at the leaf tip first: A. viridis is typically broader, oblong/ovate and blunt to shortly acute; A. asperula is typically narrower, lanceolate/linear-lanceolate and narrowly taper-pointed. Flower close-up: A. viridis corona segments are proportionally shorter than the corolla lobes. Both have hoods and neither is reliably separated by a simple 'horn present vs absent' rule. Umbel shape, soil and habit are supporting—not stand-alone—clues.

ecological_notes.host_status: High-value Monarch and Queen oviposition host in Central Texas Blackland Prairies.
ecological_notes.habitat: Prairies, pastures, glades, disturbed ground and roadsides; compared with A. asperula, often on deeper soils and valley sites, but soil preference is not an absolute diagnostic.

look_here_first: Look at a mature leaf first: usually oblong to ovate, relatively broad, with a blunt, rounded or shortly acute tip. Then check the flower: five reddish-purple hoods form the corona, but there is no conspicuous projecting horn. Compare the relatively short corona segments with the much longer pale green corolla lobes; confirm against narrow, taper-tipped A. asperula.
